title: NY State Assembly · District 80
area: The Bronx: Allerton, Morris Park, Norwood, Pelham Gardens, Pelham Parkway, and Van Nest

context.text: Both parties' primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were canceled. Incumbent John Zaccaro Jr. (D) advanced without appearing on the ballot. Denise Smith withdrew from the Republican primary but advanced from the Conservative Party primary without appearing on the ballot, so she appears on the Conservative Party line only.

summary.text: John Zaccaro Jr. is the incumbent Democratic Assembly Member for District 80 in the Bronx, first elected in 2022 and re-elected in 2024. A Bronx native, he worked as a housing organizer and in New York City government, including as Chief of Staff to City Councilmember Rafael Salamanca Jr., before joining the Assembly. His campaign website says he is running on schools and youth programs, housing stability and senior services, neighborhood safety, and constituent services.

background.text: Zaccaro was born and raised in the Bronx by a single mother and has described experiencing housing insecurity growing up. Wikipedia reports that he attended DeWitt Clinton High School and CUNY Prep.

He began his career as an intern for the New York City Council, then worked as a housing organizer helping residents fight poor living conditions and unwarranted rent increases and working with community groups to challenge landlords in court. The Bronx Times reported in 2022 that he got his start at age 20 working with then-Councilmember Fernando Cabrera.

He served as Bronx Director for Intergovernmental Affairs under New York City Schools Chancellor Carmen Fariña, and later as Chief of Staff for City Councilmember Rafael Salamanca Jr. His official biography cites over 14 years of local service to the Bronx community.
He was a member of Bronx Community Board 7 and is a member of the Pelham Parkway Neighborhood Association, according to his official biography.
In 2020 he ran for 80th Assembly District Leader with the endorsement of the Bronx Democratic Party and lost to Marcos Sierra, according to the Bronx Times.

When Nathalia Fernandez left the Assembly seat after winning the 2022 Democratic primary for State Senate, a Bronx Democratic Party vacancy committee chose Zaccaro as the party's nominee for District 80. He defeated Republican Phyllis Nastasio in the November 2022 general election and took office on January 1, 2023; Ballotpedia also lists his 2024 general-election win over Nicholas Marricco and Grace Marrero.
As of the 2025-2026 session, he sits on the Assembly's Aging, Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, Economic Development/Job Creation/Commerce and Industry, Education, Housing, and Small Business committees.

His campaign website says he has helped secure funding for schools, after-school programs, CUNY, parks, senior centers, and Mitchell-Lama developments, and that he lives in the district with his family. His official biography says he lives in the Pelham Parkway section of the Bronx with his wife and three children.

priorities.text: "In just three years, he has helped secure millions in funding and advance legislation that strengthens neighborhoods across the district," with investments listed in schools and youth programs, housing stability and senior services, community safety and mental health resources, and parks and local business corridors.

Looking ahead, his stated priorities include expanding after-school programs and school-to-career pathways, protecting Mitchell-Lama housing and supporting homeowners and tenants, investing in community-based public-safety and mental-health services, expanding senior services, and improving city and state agency responsiveness.

He announced that the 2024 state budget included new enforcement powers to revoke the tobacco, liquor, or lottery licenses of businesses that possess or sell illegal cannabis, which he described as a win against illegal smoke shops in his district.

record.text: Announced that the state budget signed in April 2024 gave localities new enforcement powers to revoke tobacco, liquor, or lottery licenses from businesses selling illegal cannabis, targeting unlicensed smoke shops in his district.
As of the 2025-2026 session, serves on the Assembly's Aging, Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, Economic Development/Job Creation/Commerce and Industry, Education, Housing, and Small Business committees.

candidates.name: Denise Smith

summary.text: Denise Smith is the Conservative Party candidate for Assembly District 80. She ran for New York City Council District 11 on the Conservative Party line in 2025. Little biographical information about her is publicly documented; she has no campaign website identified and has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey.

background.text: Smith won the Conservative Party primary for New York City Council District 11 in 2025, and in the November 2025 general election received 4.0% of the vote (1,462 votes) on the Conservative Party line, behind incumbent Eric Dinowitz (D) and Stylo A. Sapaskis (R).

She advanced from the June 2026 Conservative Party primary for Assembly District 80 without appearing on the ballot, after the primary was canceled; Ballotpedia lists her as having withdrawn from the Republican primary.

priorities.text: Senior care and nursing home oversight, including quality of care, stronger oversight, and auditing how funds are used, as described in Bronx.com coverage of her remarks to the Bronx Conservative Party.
Public safety, foster care reform, and transit issues, as described in the same Bronx.com coverage.

candidates.researchNotes: No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response, campaign website, or news coverage of policy positions could be located for Smith as of September 25, 2026. Her Ballotpedia page lists only personal and 2025 campaign social-media accounts (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok), which were inaccessible or contained no public posts on the current race. Re-checked 2026-10-19: Bronx.com's report of her January 2026 remarks to the Bronx Conservative Party contains no direct quotes from her, so no statements or positions were added; priorities are the reporter's summary.
